# Seed interface 1 fixtures (ADR 0007)

The seed is declared once by an operator's manager and may run the same image for years, so
every recovery actor must leave machine state that every seed ever shipped still reads the
same way. These fixtures are that promise, checked by
`node-agent/crates/quasar-recovery/tests/seed_contract.rs`.

- `profile-1.json` is the compiled actor profile: the container a seed creates when no
  recovery actor exists, rendered for the placeholder inputs the test uses.
- `actors/<release>/<case>/` is one machine as a released recovery actor leaves it:
  `seed.json` (absent when no actor has written one), `containers.json` (every container the
  seed can see, reduced to name, labels, state and command) and `expected.json` (what the
  seed decides; keys it leaves out are not part of the interface).

## `seed.json`, format 1

Written only by a recovery actor, atomically; read only by the seed.

```json
{"format_version":1,"installation_id":"<id>","recovery_actor_image":{"repository":"<repository>","digest":"sha256:<64 hex>"},"state":"active"}
```

`state` is `active` or `uninstalled`. A seed idles on any other `format_version`, a file that
does not parse, an unknown `state` or an image that is not a `sha256:` digest.

## Rules

- **Append, never edit.** Each release that ships a recovery actor adds
  `actors/<version>/`, and moves `CURRENT` in the test to it; the test proves that set is what
  the current actor writes. An existing directory is never changed to make a test pass: a
  change there is a new seed interface, which needs its own ADR and the owner's sign-off.
- `actors/rh06-06/` is the first set, from the first actor that writes `seed.json`, before
  any release carried one. Its `installed` case is generated by the test; the other cases are
  the states around it the interface covers (a first install, a stopped or deleted actor, a
  hand-over's kept and successor containers, a name held by something else, an uninstall).
